title: District Commission's Obligation to Direct Opposite Party

content.scenario: Rahul, a consumer, files a complaint with the District Commission against a local electronics store for selling him a defective smartphone. The Commission admits the complaint and directs the store to respond within 30 days.
content.outcome: The District Commission must direct the opposite party (the electronics store) to give their version of the case within a period of 30 days or an extended period not exceeding 15 days, as per section 38(3) of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019.

user_queries: What is the time limit for the opposite party to respond to a complaint?
Can the District Commission extend the time limit for response?
What happens if the opposite party fails to respond within the given time limit?
